subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Interpreting and interacting with earth systems

questions.q: Which catalyst is used to speed up the reaction in the Haber process?
questions.explain: The Haber process uses an iron catalyst to increase the rate of the reversible reaction between nitrogen and hydrogen.

questions.q: Which conditions are typically used for the Haber process?
questions.explain: A compromise temperature of around 450 C and a high pressure of about 200 atmospheres give a reasonable yield of ammonia at an acceptable rate.

questions.q: Which equation correctly represents the reversible reaction in the Haber process?
questions.explain: One molecule of nitrogen reacts reversibly with three molecules of hydrogen to form two molecules of ammonia.

questions.q: Which three elements are supplied by NPK fertilisers?
options: Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium... sodium and calcium
questions.explain: NPK fertilisers contain the essential plant nutrients nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of carrying out a life cycle assessment (LCA) of a product?
options: To assess the environmental impact of a product across its whole life
To measure only the cost of manufacturing the product
To decide the retail price of the product
To test the strength of the finished product
questions.explain: An LCA evaluates the environmental impact of a product from raw material extraction, through manufacture and use, to disposal.

questions.q: Which two substances are both required for iron to rust?
questions.explain: Rusting of iron only occurs when both water and oxygen are present.

questions.q: Blocks of zinc are bolted to the steel hull of a ship to stop it corroding. Why does this work?
options: Zinc is more reactive so it is oxidised in preference to the iron
Zinc is less reactive so it protects the steel by being unreactive
Zinc forms a waterproof paint layer over the steel
Zinc makes the steel more reactive so it rusts faster
questions.explain: This is sacrificial protection: the more reactive zinc corrodes instead of the iron in the steel.

questions.q: Bronze is an alloy made mainly from which two metals?
questions.explain: Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin, whereas brass is an alloy of copper and zinc.

questions.q: What is the general formula for the alkanes?
questions.explain: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with the general formula CnH2n+2.

questions.q: Which list gives the first four alkanes in order of increasing size?
questions.explain: The first four alkanes in order of increasing carbon number are methane, ethane, propane and butane.

questions.q: Crude oil is separated into fractions by fractional distillation. On which property does this separation depend?
options: The boiling points of the hydrocarbons
The reactivity of the hydrocarbons with oxygen
The solubility of the hydrocarbons in water
questions.explain: Fractions are separated because hydrocarbons of different chain length have different boiling points.

questions.q: What does cracking do to long-chain hydrocarbon molecules?
options: Breaks them into smaller, more useful alkanes and alkenes
Joins them into larger, more useful molecules
Turns them all into carbon dioxide and water
Removes all the hydrogen atoms to leave pure carbon
questions.explain: Cracking breaks large, less useful hydrocarbons into smaller alkanes and alkenes, which are more in demand.

questions.q: A hydrocarbon is cracked as follows: C10H22 → C8H18 + X. What is molecule X?
questions.explain: To balance the carbon and hydrogen atoms, X must be C2H4 (ethene), an alkene.

questions.q: Which functional group is present in every alkene?
questions.explain: Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons containing a reactive carbon–carbon double bond.

questions.q: A student shakes an unknown hydrocarbon with orange bromine water and it turns colourless. What does this show?
options: The hydrocarbon contains only carbon atoms
questions.explain: Alkenes decolourise bromine water because the C=C double bond reacts in an addition reaction, unlike saturated alkanes.

questions.q: Which two products are formed when a hydrocarbon undergoes complete combustion?
questions.explain: Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon in plenty of oxygen produces only carbon dioxide and water.

questions.q: Approximately what proportion of today's atmosphere is nitrogen?
questions.explain: The present-day atmosphere is roughly 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen, with small amounts of other gases.

questions.q: What is thought to have released the gases that formed the Earth's early atmosphere?
questions.explain: One theory is that the early atmosphere was produced by intense volcanic activity releasing gases such as carbon dioxide and water vapour.

questions.q: Which of these gases is a greenhouse gas that contributes to global warming?
questions.explain: Methane, along with carbon dioxide and water vapour, is a greenhouse gas that absorbs and re-emits heat radiation.

questions.q: A fuel contains sulfur impurities. When it is burned in a power station, which pollutant is released that causes acid rain?
questions.explain: Sulfur impurities burn to form sulfur dioxide, which dissolves in atmospheric water to produce acid rain.
